What it is & what it contains

The authorised book of the sanctioned Works Programme — the railway's annual works programme, organised by Plan Head; the document against which works expenditure is incurred. Works are itemised with outlays, with allocations for bulk and non-bulk items. All sanctioned works costing more than ₹2.5 crore, sanctioned by the Railway Board, are compiled in it.

Pink Book · Blue Book · Yellow Book · Brown Book · Orange Book · Green Book — the SRSF works book · Green Book — the Traffic Costing document · LAW Book — List of Approved Works
Issued by the Railway Board every year, after approval of the budget grants. Railways propose works through IRPSM with abstract estimates in the monsoon of the previous year.
Ch 1 Abstract of Revenue & Demand for Grants
The Railway Budget Books — the Colour Books & the LAW Book
Pink Book · Blue Book · Yellow Book · Brown Book · Orange Book · Green Book — the SRSF works book · Green Book — the Traffic Costing document · LAW Book — List of Approved Works

Its lumpsum provisions can be used for works up to ₹2.5 crore each of the specified category — the umbrella works. Sanctioned works below ₹2.5 crore are exhibited as the List of Approved Works (LAW). Projects below ₹20 crore are approved for inclusion; works above ₹20 crore are processed on file, approval conveyed by the AMs Committee. A work NOT in the Pink Book cannot be financed by re-appropriation — it must be projected under the RE and technically revived; without prior sanction it would be a new service.

Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)
Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966; in force at once. Revised on Santhanam Committee recommendations. Do not apply to All India Services members, RPF members or casual appointees (corpus).
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)

'Government' = President / Railway Board / Secretary, Railway Board / GM, as graded; 'railway servant' per IREC Rule 103(43); 'family' = spouse + wholly dependent son/daughter/step-child and dependent relatives.
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)
At all times: absolute integrity, devotion to duty, nothing unbecoming. Supervisors must ensure integrity of subordinates; superior's directions ordinarily in writing.
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)
No discourtesy in official duties; no dilatory tactics or wilful delay in disposal of work.
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)
Act per Government policies on age of marriage, environment, wildlife, cultural heritage; observe policies on prevention of crime against women.
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)
Prohibition of sexual harassment of working women
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)

No act of sexual harassment at the workplace; the in-charge must take steps to prevent it. Covers physical contact/advances, demand for sexual favours, sexually coloured remarks, showing pornography, other unwelcome conduct.
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)
Employment of near relatives in firms enjoying Government patronage
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)

No use of position/influence to secure family employment. Group A officer needs prior sanction for son/daughter/dependent joining a firm he deals with officially; family employment in any firm must be intimated; step aside from matters where family is interested.
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)
Taking part in politics and elections
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)

No membership of / association with a political party or political movement; no canvassing or use of influence in elections. Voting is allowed, without indicating the choice. Family's subversive activity must be prevented, else reported.
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)

No joining/continuing in an association whose objects/activities are prejudicial to sovereignty & integrity of India, public order or morality. A gazetted servant may not join a non-gazetted staff union; on promotion to gazetted rank he must resign (ordinary membership only in the narrow beneficent-scheme exception, with GM's satisfaction).
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)

No demonstration prejudicial to sovereignty/integrity, security of State, friendly relations, public order, decency/morality, or involving contempt of court, defamation or incitement. Peaceful lunch-interval / half-hour before-after-hours meetings without obstruction are not a breach (Ministry's decisions).
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)
Connection with press or other media
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)

No owning, conducting, editing or managing a newspaper/periodical/electronic media without previous sanction of Government. Bona fide official-duty publication excepted; own views must be stated to be his own, not Government's.
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)

No statement in broadcast, document, press communication or public utterance adversely criticising current/recent Central/State policy, or embarrassing Centre-State or Centre-foreign relations. Statements in official capacity / due performance of duty excepted.
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)

No evidence before any person/committee/authority without previous sanction; even with sanction, no criticism of Central/State policy while deposing. Excepted: enquiries by Government/Parliament/Legislature-appointed authorities, judicial enquiries, departmental enquiries.
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)
Communicate information only per the RTI Act, 2005 and its rules; no direct/indirect communication of any official document, part thereof or classified information to an unauthorised person.
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)
No asking for / accepting contributions, or associating with raising of funds or collections in cash or kind for any object, without previous sanction of Government / competent authority.
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)

General bar on accepting gifts (self, family, or anyone on his behalf). 'Gift' includes free transport, boarding, lodging, other service or pecuniary advantage from a person other than a near relative / personal friend with no official dealings. Casual meal, lift or social hospitality is not a gift. Detailed limits in the next table.
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)
No giving, taking or abetting of dowry; no demanding dowry from parents/guardian of bride or bridegroom. 'Dowry' as in the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

Public demonstrations in honour of railway servants

No complimentary/valedictory address, testimonial or entertainment in his (or another servant's) honour without previous sanction. Excepted: substantially private/informal farewell on retirement/transfer, and simple inexpensive public entertainments.
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)

Without previous sanction: no trade/business, no other employment, no elective office/canvassing, no canvassing for family insurance/commission agency, no part in registration/promotion/management of a bank/company or commercial co-operative, no sponsored media programme. Without sanction allowed: honorary social/charitable work, occasional literary/artistic/scientific work, amateur sports, literary/scientific/charitable or sports-club societies and staff co-operatives (report within 1 month where required). Family trade/business or insurance/commission agency must be reported; no fee for outside work without sanction.

Sub-letting and vacation of Government accommodation
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)
No sub-letting, leasing or allowing occupation of allotted Government accommodation by another person; vacate within the time-limit after cancellation of allotment.
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)

No speculation in any stock, share or investment — frequent purchase/sale is deemed speculation; occasional investment through authorised stock-brokers excepted. No investment likely to embarrass or influence official duty (incl. directors'/friends' quota shares; no IPO/FPO application in a CPSE whose price fixation he decides). Lending/borrowing detail in the financial-conduct table.

Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)

Manage private affairs to avoid habitual indebtedness/insolvency; forthwith report full facts of any legal proceeding for recovery of debt or for adjudging him insolvent. Burden of proving unavoidable circumstances is on the servant. Salary attachment tests (moiety frequently attached / attached over 2 years / unpayable within 2 years) expose him to dismissal/removal process.

Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)

Return of assets & liabilities on first appointment; annual immovable-property return (Group A & B, and specified Group C categories — January each year). Immovable: previous knowledge of Government; previous sanction if the other party has official dealings. Movable: report within 1 month if value exceeds 2 months' basic pay; previous sanction if the other party has official dealings. Detail in the financial-conduct table.

Immovable property outside India; transactions with foreigners
Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)

Previous sanction is compulsory to acquire/dispose of immovable property situated outside India, or to transact for such property with any foreigner / foreign Government / foreign organisation or concern.

No recourse to Court or Press to vindicate an officially criticised/defamed act without previous sanction; if no sanction is received within 3 months of the request, permission is deemed granted. Private character may be vindicated freely, with a report to Government.

Rule-wise map — Rules 1 to 22A (one line each)
No bringing (or attempt) of political or other influence on a superior to further his service interests.

No marriage with a person having a living spouse; no second marriage while a spouse is living — Government may permit only where the personal law allows and grounds exist. Marriage to a person of other than Indian nationality must be intimated forthwith.

Abide by the law on intoxicating drinks/drugs on duty; no consumption in a public place, no appearing intoxicated in public, no excess. Running staff and staff directly connected with train passing: no drink/drug within 8 hours before commencement of duty or during duty.

Speculation in stocks/shares/investments barred; frequent purchase or sale = speculation. Occasional investment through duly authorised/licensed stock-brokers is allowed.

Save in the ordinary course of business with a bank or a public limited company: no lending/borrowing/deposit, as principal or agent, with any person/firm/private limited company he is likely to have official dealings with; no lending money at interest or for a return in money/kind. Excepted: purely temporary small interest-free loan to/from a relative or personal friend; credit account with a bona fide tradesman; advance/pay to a private employee; transactions with previous sanction. Loan from LIC against own policy needs no permission (Ministry's decision).

Avoid habitual indebtedness/insolvency; report debt-recovery/insolvency proceedings forthwith. Attachment markers: moiety of pay frequently attached, continuously attached for over 2 years, or attached for a sum not repayable within 2 years.

On first appointment: return of assets & liabilities (immovable property; shares, debentures, cash incl. bank deposits; other movable property; debts/liabilities). Movable items under ₹10,000 may be lumped; daily-use articles need not be included. Annual immovable-property return: Group A & B every year; specified Group C supervisory staff (return in January; first return within 3 months of appointment in the grade) and listed commercial staff (also on every promotion and ~2 years before superannuation).

Previous KNOWLEDGE of Government is required for any lease, mortgage, purchase, sale, gift or other transaction, in own or family member's name. Previous SANCTION is required if the transaction is with a person having official dealings with him. Building a house: report/seek permission before starting, report after completion; sanction needed if repairs/minor construction is estimated to exceed ₹1,000 (Ministry's decision).

REPORT to Government within 1 month of the transaction if its value exceeds 2 months' basic pay (ACS No. 118, RBE No. 105/2011). Previous sanction if the other party has official dealings with him. 'Movable property' includes jewellery, insurance policies whose annual premium exceeds 2 months' basic pay, shares, securities and debentures, all loans, motor cars/cycles, horses/conveyance, refrigerators, radios, TV sets.
Shares / securities / debentures / mutual funds — cumulative in a calendar year

Separate intimation in the prescribed proforma (in addition to Rule 18(3) reports): Group A & B — cumulative sale/purchase exceeding ₹50,000 in the calendar year; Group C & D — exceeding ₹25,000 in the calendar year.

No fee for work for any private/public body or private person without sanction of the prescribed authority. Report if any family member is engaged in trade/business or owns/manages an insurance or commission agency.

The Traffic Book — Parts A to D

Consolidated station accounts of the railway — every station’s monthly Balance Sheet (Coaching and Goods separately; luggage in a separate balance sheet) converted into one horizontal, consolidated statement. Debit side: opening balance + the month’s earnings (tickets sold, to-pay invoices, parcels, demurrage/wharfage accrued, sundry earnings); credit side: cash remitted, vouchers and credits accepted by the Accounts Office. The opening balance of a month is the previous month’s closing balance — station outstandings roll forward until realised. Postings are made from station returns after the Traffic Accounts Office’s internal check (Error Sheets; Advice of Internal Check A.2751/A.2754); if a balance sheet is missing, an approximate one is prepared. Part A totals must agree with the station balance sheets in aggregate.

The Traffic Book — Parts A to D

Apportionment of through-traffic earnings is worked in this Part — it carries the net results of apportionment. The through earning is first taken into the Traffic Account/Suspense; terminal charges (passenger terminal charges 5%, received only by the originating railway) and transhipment charges (to the home railway performing it) are taken out before division. Never apportioned — retained by the collecting railway: excess fare, luggage (apportionment 0%), animals and birds, TTE collections; Blank Paper Ticket (BPT) earnings ARE apportioned. The balance (pure line-haul) is divided pro-rata to the distance carried on each railway. Apportionment is centralised — worked by CRIS on distance, co-ordinated by Western Railway as the nodal railway. The net result is transferred to / received from foreign railways through the Account Current; the operating ratio is calculated on apportioned earnings.

The Traffic Book — Parts A to D

The home railway’s ledger in the traffic books — the Traffic Account (Suspense) is operated in this Part, under Major Heads 1002/1003. It holds earnings transactions pending final adjustment — unrealised accrued earnings parked until each item is final. Components: Accounts Receivable, Inward Paid, Special Accounts and Traffic Book differences (Bills Recoverable is NOT a component). Balance is always debit. In the monthly cycle (IPAS), station/division collections are credited into it and posted out to the abstract-wise earnings heads; the GST embedded in earnings is taken to the Deposit Misc heads. The closing balance represents unrealised earnings; the PFA prepares clearance estimates and the Railway Board fixes yearly clearance targets.

The Traffic Book — Parts A to D

The closing Part — earnings summarised by abstract: Abstract X (Coaching), Abstract Y (Goods), Abstract Z (Sundry), with the statement of balances. Balances of the Accounts Office Balance Sheet (AOB, Form A.2923 — traffic cash received otherwise than through a station balance sheet) are entailed here. It is the reconciliation / miscellaneous Part and the link to the General Books — the difference between earnings as per the Traffic Book and as per the General Books is explained by Cash in Transit. Earnings (Abstracts X, Y, Z) pass into the Monthly Account Current, which must reach the Railway Board by the 8th of the following month.
